title: Docker Installation and First Containers
moduleObjectives: Install Docker Engine from the official Docker apt repository, including the GPG key and repository setup
Add your user to the `docker` group so Docker commands run without `sudo`
Run `docker run hello-world` and explain the pull, create, run, and exit sequence Docker performs
Run an nginx container in detached mode with a port mapping and reach it from a browser
Distinguish images from containers and clean up both with `docker rm`, `docker rmi`, and the prune commands
Manage and inspect containers and images from the VS Code Docker sidebar

lessons.title: Setup Check
lessons.objective: Verify the Ubuntu environment is ready for Docker installation by checking Linux, sudo, the curl and gpg packages, network reachability of Docker Hub, and free disk space.

lessons.title: Install Docker Engine
lessons.objective: Install Docker Engine from the official Docker apt repository and add your user to the docker group so `docker info` works without sudo.

lessons.title: Your First Container
lessons.objective: Run the hello-world container and explain the six steps Docker performed, from pulling the image off Docker Hub to the container exiting.

lessons.title: Running a Real Image
lessons.objective: Run an nginx web server as a detached, port-mapped, named container, reach it from a browser, and inspect it with `docker logs` and `docker exec`.

lessons.title: Images vs Containers
lessons.objective: Distinguish images from containers by running multiple containers from one image, then clean up both with `docker rm`, `docker rmi`, and the prune commands.

lessons.title: The VS Code Docker Sidebar
lessons.objective: Manage containers and images from the VS Code Docker sidebar, including stopping, removing, viewing logs, and attaching a shell via the right-click menu.

lessons.title: Final Checkpoint
lessons.objective: Demonstrate module mastery by running, verifying, and cleaning up a named detached nginx container end-to-end without instructor help.

quiz.question: During the setup check, you run `which docker` before installing anything. What result tells you that you are ready to proceed?
options: The path `/usr/bin/docker` is printed
A Docker version string is printed
No output at all — Docker should not be installed yet
The message `Active: active (running)`
quiz.feedback: The lesson expects no output from `which docker`, because Docker is about to be installed and any existing installation needs to be flagged first.

quiz.question: After running `sudo usermod -aG docker $USER`, `docker info` still fails with "permission denied while trying to connect to the Docker daemon socket". What fixes this?
options: Run `newgrp docker` or log out and back in to refresh group membership
Reinstall Docker Engine with `sudo apt install --reinstall docker-ce`
Run `sudo apt update` and try again
Add the docker group to `/etc/apt/sources.list.d/docker.list`
quiz.feedback: Group membership only takes effect in a new session, so the lesson has you run `newgrp docker` or log out and back in before Docker works without sudo.

quiz.question: Why does the installation lesson download Docker's GPG key to `/etc/apt/keyrings/docker.asc` before adding the apt repository?
options: So you can log in to Docker Hub without a password
To prove the packages you download are really from Docker
To encrypt images that Docker pulls from the registry
So Docker commands can run without sudo
quiz.feedback: The lesson explains the GPG key proves the packages you download are genuinely from Docker.

quiz.question: The first time you run `docker run hello-world`, the output starts with "Unable to find image 'hello-world:latest' locally". What does this line mean?
options: The installation failed and Docker cannot find its own files
You typed the image name wrong and need to retry
The Docker daemon is not running and must be started
It is not an error — Docker did not have the image cached, so it pulled it from Docker Hub
quiz.feedback: The lesson stresses this line is not an error: Docker checked locally, found nothing, and pulled the image from Docker Hub before running it.

quiz.question: You ran `docker run hello-world` twice, but `docker ps` shows nothing. Why?
options: The containers were automatically deleted when they finished
`docker ps` only shows running containers, and the hello-world containers exited; `docker ps -a` shows them
hello-world runs entirely in memory and never creates a container
You need sudo to see containers with `docker ps`
quiz.feedback: By default `docker ps` lists only running containers; the exited hello-world containers are still on disk and appear with `docker ps -a`.

quiz.question: In the command `docker run -d -p 8080:80 --name web nginx`, what does `-p 8080:80` do?
options: Forwards port 8080 on your machine to port 80 inside the container
Forwards port 80 on your machine to port 8080 inside the container
Makes nginx listen on both ports 8080 and 80 inside the container
Limits the container to 8080 KB of memory on port 80
quiz.feedback: The lesson explains `-p 8080:80` maps host port 8080 to container port 80, where nginx listens, so you reach it at localhost:8080.

quiz.question: Which command opens an interactive shell inside the running container named `web`?
options: `docker shell web`
`docker run -it web bash`
`docker exec -it web bash`
`docker logs -f web`
quiz.feedback: The lesson uses `docker exec -it web bash` to get a shell inside the running container; the prompt changes to root inside the container's filesystem.

quiz.question: What is the difference between `docker rm` and `docker rmi`?
options: `docker rm` removes running containers; `docker rmi` removes stopped ones
`docker rm` removes an image; `docker rmi` removes a container
They are aliases and do exactly the same thing
`docker rm` removes a container; `docker rmi` removes an image
quiz.feedback: As the lesson's quick reference states, `docker rm <name>` removes a stopped container while `docker rmi <image>` removes an image.

quiz.question: What does `docker container prune -f` do?
options: Stops all running containers
Removes all stopped containers in one step
Removes all images not used by any container
Removes both containers and their images
quiz.feedback: The lesson introduces `docker container prune -f` as the shortcut that removes all stopped containers at once; images require `docker image prune -a`.

quiz.question: According to the VS Code Docker sidebar lesson, which task is better done with the CLI than the sidebar?
options: Running a container with specific port mappings and a custom name
Seeing what is running right now at a glance
Inspecting a container's environment variables and mounts
Opening a container's logs in an editor tab
quiz.feedback: The lesson's comparison table says the sidebar's Run option loses control over flags like `-p` and `--name`, so running with specific port mappings is better in the CLI.
